hook.say: This morning, we looked at OpenAI putting the Decisions API into public beta for typed decision flows in production. I went back in to check the pricing, the direct benchmark, and one product limit.

findings.label: PRICE
findings.headline: Measured cost per call was 2.1× Jev in one benchmark
findings.detail: Same workload, 2,759 calls, with both vendors’ own token counts.
findings.evidence: Per 1,000 calls: $0.22 for the Decisions API against $0.11 for Jev.
findings.say: First, an independent benchmark measured the Decisions API at 2.1 times the cost per call versus Jev on the same workload.

findings.label: LATENCY
findings.headline: At p99, the slow tail was 1,469 ms vs 526 ms
findings.detail: Median latency was basically tied, but tail latency was wider for Decisions.
findings.evidence: At the 99th percentile it is 1,469 ms against 526 ms, 2.8× slower.
findings.say: Second, the same test says median speed was basically tied, but at p99 the Decisions API had a much longer tail.

findings.label: LIMIT
findings.headline: API reference shows no external image URLs or file IDs
findings.detail: Image input exists, but only inline image payloads are documented today.
findings.evidence: An inline image. External URLs and file IDs are not supported.
findings.say: Third, the API supports images, but the reference says external image URLs and file IDs are not supported right now.

take.headline: Good for routing, but measure the tails
take.say: My take: typed decisions are useful, but shipping means checking latency tails, real call cost, and operational limits before wiring it into production.

sources.title: Nexus Agent — OpenAI Decisions API vs Jev

caption:
This morning, I showed why OpenAI’s Decisions API matters: it gives production workflows a typed decision layer instead of just another agent reply.

2.1× measured cost per call vs Jev on one 2,759-call benchmark.
1,469 ms p99 latency vs 526 ms in that same head-to-head test.
Image support is there, but the reference says no external image URLs or file IDs.

My take: production AI is not about sounding smart. It is about measuring cost, tails, and limits before the decision touches the operation.

Comment AGENTES and I will send you the details by DM.
